original_value: Multi-view sequential learning is a fundamental problem in machine learning dealing with multi-view sequences. In a multi-view sequence, there exists two forms of interactions between different views: view-specific interactions and cross-view interactions. In this paper, we present a new neural architecture for multi-view sequential learning called the Memory Fusion Network (MFN) that explicitly accounts for both interactions in a neural architecture and continuously models them through time. The first component of the MFN is called the System of LSTMs, where view-specific interactions are learned in isolation through assigning an LSTM function to each view. The cross-view interactions are then identified using a special attention mechanism called the Delta-memory Attention Network (DMAN) and summarized through time with a Multi-view Gated Memory. Through extensive experimentation, MFN is compared to various proposed approaches for multi-view sequential learning on multiple publicly available benchmark datasets. MFN outperforms all the multi-view approaches. Furthermore, MFN outperforms all current state-of-the-art models, setting new state-of-the-art results for all three multi-view datasets.

result.paraphrase: Multi-view sequential learning is a core machine learning problem concerned with sequences that contain multiple views. Such sequences involve two kinds of interactions among views: view-specific interactions and cross-view interactions. In this paper, we introduce a new neural architecture for multi-view sequential learning, the Memory Fusion Network (MFN), which explicitly captures both interaction types and models them continuously over time. Its first module, the System of LSTMs, learns view-specific interactions independently by assigning an LSTM to each view. Cross-view interactions are then detected with a dedicated attention mechanism, the Delta-memory Attention Network (DMAN), and aggregated over time using a Multi-view Gated Memory. Using extensive experiments on multiple publicly available benchmark datasets, MFN is evaluated against various proposed multi-view sequential learning methods. MFN surpasses all multi-view approaches. It also outperforms all existing state-of-the-art models, establishing new state-of-the-art results on all three multi-view datasets.
